brief: My balcony is full sun with moderate moisture, and a cat and a dog live in the household. A sunny balcony and one cat. I would like some cat grass for her to nibble on.

design.site_summary: A full sun, moderately moist balcony inhabited by a curious cat and dog.
design.layout_strategy: The scheme stacks in three distinct layers: tall architectural grasses anchor the mid-height containers against the sunny wall, aromatic foliage spills from mid-level pots, and a dedicated low wooden tray at floor level provides accessible grazing for the cat.
design.combination_logic: The design contrasts the fine, upright, linear blades of Lemon Grass and Sudan Grass with the soft, textured mounds of Catnip, creating a dynamic interplay of vertical lines and bushy volumes. The colour palette is a rich tapestry of fresh greens and silvery-grey tones, offering strong textural contrast and seasonal movement as the grasses sway in the breeze.

zones.placement: On the balcony floor in a sheltered corner, receiving 6 hours of full sun.

plants.why: Provides safe, fast-growing grass blades specifically for the cat to nibble.
plants.role_in_combination: Acts as the low, accessible focal point for the pet, offering a soft vertical grass texture right at floor level.

maintenance: Water every two days to keep the soil consistently moist for rapid grass regeneration.
Trim back older grass blades weekly to encourage fresh, tender growth.
Reseed the shallow tray every 4 to 6 weeks as the annual grass completes its lifecycle.

zones.placement: In large containers against the back wall, enjoying full sun and brilliant light exposure.

plants.why: Thrives in full sun and provides a stunning structural evergreen clump.
plants.role_in_combination: Provides height, architectural contrast, and a refreshing citrus scent that complements the surrounding foliage.

plants.why: Adds height and tropical flair while tolerating the sunny microclimate.
plants.role_in_combination: Serves as the primary vertical anchor of the mid-tier, contrasting sharply with the fine textures of the grasses.

maintenance: Water thoroughly twice a week during peak summer, reducing to weekly in autumn.
Apply a balanced liquid fertilizer monthly throughout the spring and summer growing season.
Remove lower brown leaves in autumn to keep stems clean and prevent pest hiding spots.

zones.placement: In mid-sized pots flanking the larger structural grasses, soaking up full sun.

plants.why: Loves full sun to partial shade and delights the household cat.
plants.role_in_combination: Contributes a soft, mounding grey-green habit and delicate lavender flowers that soften the hard edges of the containers.

maintenance: Water when the top two inches of soil feel dry, roughly twice a week in summer.
Prune back by one third after flowering in mid-summer to promote a second flush of growth.
Divide overcrowded pots every spring to maintain vigorous growth.

care_instructions.task: Check soil moisture in all containers and thoroughly water until drainage occurs from the base.
care_instructions.frequency: Twice a week in summer, weekly in spring and autumn

care_instructions.task: Apply a slow-release organic granular fertilizer to the mid-tier containers to support vigorous grass and palm growth.
Inspect the Sudan Grass grazing tray and replant fresh seed if the old grass becomes depleted or trampled.

care_cautions: Ensure toxic non-catalogue plants like Nightshade are strictly kept off the balcony, as curious pets may ingest them.
The Sudan Grass in the ground zone may dry out very quickly in intense full sun and requires diligent watering compared to the deeper containers.
design.pet_safety_note: The design includes a dedicated, non-toxic grazing station stocked with Sudan Grass and Catnip to satisfy the cat's natural urge to nibble, while keeping structural plants secure in heavy mid-tier pots.
